name: Biscayne Park Village Commission

meetings.pattern: First Tuesday of the month, 6:00 p.m., Log Cabin, 640 NE 114th Street, Biscayne Park, FL 33161; moved to the second Tuesday when the first conflicts (January, August and November 2026). Zoom link printed on agendas.

schedule.note: Scheduled for the second Tuesday due to the General Election on Tuesday, November 3, 2026

phases.name: Tentative millage special meeting and budget workshops (2025 pattern)
phases.decides: In 2025 the commission set the waste fee and tentative millage at a July 17 special meeting and held budget workshops August 14 and 26, all at 6 p.m. The 2026 dates were not found on a fetchable page.

phases.name: First and final budget hearings (2025 pattern)
phases.decides: In 2025: first budget hearing September 9 at 6 p.m., final budget hearing (tentative) September 24 at 6 p.m. The 2026 hearing dates were not found; the 2026 schedule PDF lists only regular meetings.

phases.name: Fiscal year begins
phases.decides: Not confirmed on a fetchable village page; September hearings imply the Florida standard October 1 start. Treat as unverified.

phases.name: Village commission election
phases.decides: Seats on the Village Commission; the 2026 Notice of Candidacy form names the November 3, 2026 election. Number of seats and candidates were not readable.

levers.how: Speak during the 'Public Comments' item near the top of the regular agenda at the Log Cabin or through the Zoom link printed on the agenda; the commission then has a 'Commission Reply to Comments' item.
levers.rules: No time limit or sign-up rule is printed on the agendas or minutes read (2022, 2023, 2025). The village's rules page could not be fetched (robots).

levers.how: No written comment procedure is published. Email the Village Clerk, Pamela Latimore, at villageclerk@biscayneparkfl.gov or Village Hall at villagehall@biscayneparkfl.gov.
Call Village Hall at 305-899-8000 or email villagehall@biscayneparkfl.gov; the Mayor and Commissioners page lists members but blocked automated fetching.
Ask the Village Clerk at villageclerk@biscayneparkfl.gov or 305-899-8000.

Charter amendment by petition is available under state law: a petition signed by 10 percent of the registered electors as of the last municipal general election forces a referendum at the next general election or a special election.
levers.rules: Fla. Stat. 166.031(1). The village charter (2006, manager-commission form) is linked from the village site as 'Charter (Founding Document)' but that page and municode.com both blocked automated fetching, so any charter initiative section is not recorded.

levers.how: Not found. The charter was not readable (see petition); only the state charter-amendment referendum route under Fla. Stat. 166.031 is confirmed.

Recall follows Florida's uniform municipal recall statute, which applies to every city whether or not its charter has a recall section. For a village with 2,000 to 4,999 registered electors the first petition needs the greater of 250 electors or 10 percent, gathered within 30 days; for 500 to 1,999, the greater of 100 or 10 percent. A second 'Recall Petition and Defense' round needs 15 percent within 60 days.
levers.rules: Fla. Stat. 100.361(1), (2)(b), (2)(f), (3)(a), (3)(c), (11), (12). File with the Village Clerk. Elector count not checked; pick the tier from county registration figures.
levers.deadline: 30 days for the first round; 60 days for the second

levers.how: File the Notice of Candidacy form with the Village Clerk; candidates must meet all Charter qualifications. The 2026 qualifying dates were not found on a fetchable page.
Vote in the November 3, 2026 commission election; the county handles registration, ballots and tallying while the Village Clerk runs the election.
levers.rules: Registered voters living in the village.

levers.how: Apply for a seat on a village board (Arts and Culture, Code Compliance, Parks and Parkways, Planning and Design Review, Sustainability and Resiliency) through the 'Apply for a Board or Committee Position' link on the Government page.

elections.terms: Not confirmed from a current page. A 2009 village newsletter described three commission seats filled each election, with the two highest vote-getters getting four-year terms and the third a two-year term; the county municipality directory lists the next election as November 2026, and the 2026 Notice of Candidacy names November 3, 2026.
